thread:
incident_bot: PAGER: P0 - GPU capacity exhaustion detected in us-west-2-hosted. Autoscaler hitting scale limit, queue backlog growing. Alert routed to #incidents and on-call. Details: cluster=redwood-usw2, pool=hosted-gpu-pool, metric=gpu.available, threshold=10%

platform_pager: Confirming, dashboards show free GPUs <8% for last 8m, token-gen queue size jumped from 120 -> 420 in 6m. Seen a bunch of small MIG slices preventing binpacking.

sre_oncall_1: Ack. I'm on it. First pass: validate autoscaler errors and whether there are failed launches. `kubectl get hpa -n inference` showed nothing obvious but pool autoscaler logs show repeated placement failures. Pulling scheduler logs now.

eng_runtime: fyi we've got several 80GB jobs pinned to MIG 7g.1 configs; those aren't packing well with 40GB workloads. Likely fragmentation.

ml_infra_rahul: Logs from scheduler: "unable to allocate: insufficient contiguous cuda-slices" and repeated "MigSizeMismatch" warnings. Also noticed nodegroup scalingMax at 50 — we've hit that limit.

platform_pager: Copy. Customer impact: 5 hosted customers reporting timeouts (500s), average token latency spiked 3x. Throttling rules triggered for low-tier plans (503s). Preparing a short message for CS.

cust_success_amy: Please tag affected customers: acme-ai, travellytics, docspro. They reported degraded responses since ~09:12 UTC. I'm preparing a status note.

sre_oncall_1: Quick mitigation plan - 1) temporarily allow CPU fallback for small jobs (<512 tokens) 2) eject a few underutilized nodes to force repack 3) increase nodegroup max to 70 as emergency lift 4) manual MIG slice resize for 7g.1 -> 7g.2 for some nodes. Doing 1 and 3 now.

eng_runtime: For (1) config flag is `infer.fallback.cpu_on_fragmentation=true`. I'll flip it for the hosted pool. Command: `curl -XPOST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS" https://api.redwood.internal/configs/pool/hosted-gpu-pool -d '{"fallback_cpu":true}'`

platform_pager: Executing scale up: `cloudctl nodegroup set-max --name hosted-gpu-usw2 --max 70` (started) — this will take ~4-6m.

ml_infra_rahul: I'm triggering a rebalance job to drain low-util nodes: `schedulerctl rebalance --pool hosted-gpu-pool --strategy force-repack` — will iterate pods with <10% utilization. Expect some additional short-lived OOM/kick events.

sre_oncall_1: Noted. I'm watching queue length and autoscaler logs. Autoscaler still logging placement failures due to fragmented MIGs; rebalance might free contiguous slices.

incident_bot: NOTE: autoscaler error flood: "no suitable node found for allocation" at 09:18:42 UTC (x211). Escalation threshold hit.

eng_runtime: Quick debug snippet for scheduler log (tail):
```
2026-03-15T09:17:54Z scheduler ERROR allocate: node-37: available_slices=[0,1,0,1], required=2 contiguous
2026-03-15T09:18:01Z scheduler WARN MigSizeMismatch: requested=7g.1 available=7g.2
2026-03-15T09:18:14Z autoscaler ERROR launch failed: InsufficientCapacity
```

ml_infra_rahul: Trying manual resize on two nodes: `migctl resize node-80 --from 7g.1 --to 7g.2` — applying to nodes with mixed small-job load.

platform_pager: Scale up is progressing. New instances started but they come up without MIG fragments yet — need the scheduler to pack. Rebalance job in flight.

cust_success_amy: Draft status update for customers: "We're mitigating a GPU capacity issue affecting hosted inference in us-west-2. Some requests are delayed or receiving 503s. We're scaling and repacking clusters; ETA ~20-40m. We'll post updates here." Approve?

sre_oncall_1: Approving. Add note: customers with heavy streaming workloads may see partial degraded quality due to CPU fallback.

eng_runtime: Observed another pattern: long-running KV-cache sessions are pinning large slices. Suggest aborting idle sessions older than 10m for the next 30m window: `cachectl expire --idle 10m --pool hosted-gpu-pool`

platform_pager: Doing that now. Running `cachectl` returned ~120 sessions expired. Should free some KV in 60-120s.

ml_infra_rahul: Rebalance logs show progressive improvement, placement failures dropped by ~60% after repack start. Queue stopped growing at 430 and now slowly trending down.

incident_bot: Customer-impact summary (automated): affected_requests=~18k, error_rate=12.4%, avg_latency=3.1s -> 1.9s delta vs baseline. Top customers: acme-ai, travellytics, docspro.

sre_oncall_1: Next step: if queue >300 after 30m, we'll enable emergency oversubscribe policy to allow smaller non-critical jobs on shared GPUs (risk: potential slowdowns). Also preparing an incident retrospective ticket.

sre_oncall_2: I'm taking handoff at 09:35 UTC. Current state on handoff: autoscaler max bumped to 70, rebalance running, CPU fallback enabled, cache expired, manual MIG resizes applied to 2 nodes, queue ~290 and dropping. Please include actions taken in the incident timeline.

sre_oncall_1: Handoff acknowledged. Key mitigations to carry forward: monitor for re-fragmentation, coordinate with capacity planning to adjust MIG mix (add more 40GB-equivalent instances), follow up with sales/CS on customer credits.

cust_success_amy: Posted status update to customers and created follow-up for credits for affected tenants.

platform_pager: I will open a postmortem and schedule a runbook update to include auto-resize heuristics and emergency nodegroup increase steps. Also propose defaulting to mixed MIG sizes in new clusters to reduce fragmentation risk.

ml_infra_rahul: Leaving a note for infra: consider an automated repack cron during low-traffic windows and a probe that fails new small-slice launches if fragmented density > 0.6.

sre_oncall_2: Closing this thread for now; will reopen if metrics regress. All teams stand by in #eng-runtime and #support.

incident_bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity=P0 -> status=mitigated; mitigation_window_started=09:18 UTC; current_status=monitoring
